title: 11 Best Herbal Creams For Phlegm
intro: Herbal creams for Phlegm are topical preparations derived from plants and herbs, used to relieve and treat the symptoms of phlegm accumulation in the body, such as congestion, coughing, and difficulty breathing. These creams offer several benefits, including reducing inflammation and promoting drainage, thereby providing quick relief from phlegm-related discomfort. Popular examples of herbal creams for phlegm treatment include Eucalyptus cream, which eases congestion and opens airways, Peppermint cream, which cools and soothes the skin, and Ginger cream, which reduces inflammation and fights infection. Other effective herbal creams include Thyme cream, which has antibacterial properties and helps to clear mucus, Echinacea cream, which boosts the immune system and fights off infection, and Turmeric cream, which reduces inflammation and promotes healing.

preparations.preparation_desc: Eucalyptus globulus creams have been traditionally used to treat the phlegm ailment due to their decongestant and expectorant properties, which help to relieve congestion and promote the removal of excess mucus from the respiratory tract. The herbal preparation contains bioactive constituents such as eucalyptol, cineole, and limonene, which exhibit anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial activities that aid in reducing phlegm production and soothing the mucous membranes. The application of Eucalyptus globulus creams helps to thin out the mucus, making it easier to expel, thereby providing quick relief from coughs and congestion associated with phlegm ailments. Regular use of these creams can also help to prevent the recurrence of phlegm-related respiratory issues, offering long-term benefits for individuals suffering from this condition.
preparations.preparation_study: According to "Zhongguo Zhong yao za zhi = Zhongguo zhongyao zazhi = China journal of Chinese materia medica", Eucalyptus globulus creams for phlegm have shown to inhibit hypersecretion of airway mucins, significantly reducing mucin content in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid and MUC5ac expression in trachea and bronchiole epithelium.

The bioactive constituents of Rosmarinus officinalis creams, including camphor, borneol, and rosmarinic acid, contribute to their therapeutic effects by inhibiting the production of mucus and reducing inflammation. The benefits of using Rosmarinus officinalis creams to treat the phlegm ailment include rapid relief from symptoms, improved respiratory function, and a reduced risk of complications such as bronchitis and pneumonia.
